title: Recruiter
description: Own Kairos’s hiring and build a recruiting process that can keep up with our rapid growth. We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis. About Kairos Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs: SPAR : The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others. Generator Residency : In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more. Global Challenges Project : A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. Pathfinder Fellowship : Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work. We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem. The Role Who we hire over the next year, and how quickly we hire them, will shape which programs Kairos can run and how ambitious they can be. Until now, our hiring has been run by our co-directors and a few staff alongside their other work, so we’re looking for a recruiter to take it on full time. You’d run our hiring rounds, find strong candidates, and build the processes that let us hire well as we grow. What You’ll Do Run Kairos’s hiring rounds end to end. You’ll manage every stage of the pipeline, including application review, work tests, interviews, reference checks, work trials, and offers. Source candidates. Many of our best hires have come to us through people we know, so you’ll draw on our programs, our network, and the broader ecosystem to find strong candidates. Build and improve our hiring infrastructure. You’ll design and refine applications, work tests, interview questions, and candidate tracking. You’ll also think a lot about how AI is changing the way people apply and how we can use it to run hiring better. Help build the team. Beyond running hiring processes, you’ll help scope new roles and weigh in on org design questions, like who we need next and how roles should fit together. Support hiring for Kairos Labs. Kairos Labs, our upcoming incubator for new AI safety organizations, plans to launch in early 2027, and you may help the organizations it supports find their first hires. Who You Are Experience with recruiting. Ideally you’ve run hiring processes before, whether as a recruiter or in a role where hiring was a big part of your work. Strong judgment about people. You’ll make many calls about who should move forward, and you should be comfortable making them well under uncertainty. Good with people. Candidates should enjoy talking with you and come away excited about Kairos. Organized and reliable. We often have 5–10 hiring rounds running at once, so you’ll need to keep track of candidates, interviews, work tests, and work trials across all of them without dropping balls. Mission-aligned with context on AI safety. You care deeply about making advanced AI go well, and you have enough context on the ecosystem to recognize promising people and understand what our roles need. Why Work With Us You’ll be working toward reducing risks from advanced AI, potentially the most important challenge of our time. The people you help us hire over the next year will determine how ambitious Kairos can be, including our capacity to launch new, impactful projects and grow the programs we already run. You’d be Kairos’s first dedicated recruiter, with a lot of room to shape how we hire. We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact. Collaborate regularly with leading AI safety researchers, policy professionals, funders, and organizers. What We Offer Salary : $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates Location : This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses. Benefits : Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture. Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered. Logistics Start date : Flexible, though we generally expect new hires to be able to start within a couple of months of applying Remote, with expected travel 3–6 times a year for conferences and events, predominantly in the US We’d also be happy for you to work out of any of the AI safety hubs in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston. We prefer candidates who can attend meetings in the ET time zone (though our team currently spans GMT-8 to GMT+1). Kairos is happy to sponsor visas to the US (typically H-1Bs or O-1As) and will likely be able to sponsor UK visas in the coming months. We can’t guarantee visa approvals, however. Our Culture We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem. We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard. Application Process We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis. Application form (10–20 mins) Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid) Interview (45 mins) Reference checks Work trial (3 days, paid) Offer If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for. This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply. AI tools help us review applications. If we receive more apps than we can read, some may be declined based on the AI review alone. Learn more → Questions? Reach out at Know someone who might be a good fit? If your referral gets hired and completes two months with us, we’ll pay you a $10,000 referral bonus. Learn more here . What We Offer

The Role

The Global Challenges Project (GCP) runs three-day residential workshops that help talented individuals explore careers in AI safety and biosecurity. Over the past few years, GCP has run dozens of workshops for 400+ students, mostly in Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. GCP has a long and successful track record and became part of Kairos in early 2026.

We’re now expanding GCP into a full portfolio of workshops serving different audiences and career stages, with the ambition of becoming the leading fieldbuilding workshop organizer in AI safety and biosecurity. This means building new programs, new formats, and the systems to deliver reliably at scale.

We’re looking for a GCP Program Manager to build and lead at least two strands of our expanding workshop portfolio, reporting to Sam Glendenning, who leads the Global Challenges Project.

You’ll have broad ownership of your programs, from deciding what they should achieve and who they should serve through to delivering the workshops themselves. This includes outreach and marketing strategy, participant selection, guest recruitment, workshop design, team leadership, in-person delivery, and impact evaluation.

This is an unusually hands-on role. You’ll shape the strategy behind your programs, build the systems needed to run them effectively, and then lead them in person. Because we run our portfolio experimentally, individual programs may change or be discontinued, but this role is not tied to any single program. You’ll own a portfolio that evolves as we learn what works.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own two or more GCP programs. You’ll take responsibility for their strategy, design, delivery, and evaluation. Programs you may own include:

    • Workshops for students newer to AI safety, for professionals considering a pivot into AI safety, or for accelerating people into politics or policy

    • Workshop support for other organizations, from advice and coordination to running workshops on their behalf

    • A high-impact format you propose (we’re open to strong cases for new programs)

  • Run programs experimentally. We’re testing which of these programs offer the most value to the ecosystem. You’ll experiment with both the format and purpose of your workshops, and be willing to discontinue programs that aren’t working, even after investing significant time in them.

  • Own outreach and participant selection. You’ll develop marketing and outreach strategies, build strong applicant pools, and decide who will benefit most from attending each program.

  • Build relationships and recruit guests. High-quality guests are central to the impact of our workshops. You’ll proactively build relationships across the field and invite researchers, policymakers, funders, operators, and other experts to participate.

  • Design excellent workshops. You’ll develop the structure, sessions, content, and participant experience for each program, holding everything to a very high standard.

  • Lead workshops in person. You’ll give talks, introduce guests, advise participants, manage the team on the ground, and take responsibility for how well each workshop runs.

  • Lead your program teams. We organize delivery program by program. You’ll direct the work of the GCP team, interns, and volunteers on your programs (typically three to four people per workshop). Once the team grows, you’ll likely line-manage one GCP team member and our interns.

  • Measure impact and iterate. You’ll collect structured feedback at every workshop, track participant outcomes over the following months, and use the evidence to improve, scale, or discontinue programs.

  • Help GCP scale. You’ll contribute to team-wide strategy, build operational structures and automation that let us expand without compromising quality, and help design and launch our internship program.

 

Who You Are

  • Experienced at running events. You’ve organized and delivered events such as workshops, conferences, or retreats, and you’re comfortable making game-time decisions. Strong project delivery experience in complex in-person settings can substitute.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about how the development of advanced AI and biotechnology plays out, and you believe workshops can be a highly effective way to help talented people enter these fields.

  • Good with people, and energized by workshops. Leading three-day residential events is central to this role. You’ll need the energy to engage with participants and guests throughout while keeping the event running smoothly.

  • Comfortable managing a small team. Within a year, you’ll likely begin managing 2 or more people. Prior experience managing operational or programmatic teams is a strong plus.

  • High agency. You’ll have significant ownership over your programs, and we expect you to spot problems early, adapt when plans change, and fix things without waiting to be asked.

  • Highly organized. You’ll oversee several programs simultaneously, each with different workstreams, teams, and deadlines. You’ll need strong systems for keeping everything on track.

  • Familiar with the AI safety ecosystem. You know the major organizations and people in the field and understand how its parts fit together. You use that context to make good strategic decisions and to point participants toward the right opportunities. Familiarity with biosecurity or US policy is a plus, and matters more for some programs than others.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll work toward reducing risks from advanced AI and biotechnology, two of the most important challenges of our time. Both fields need far more talented people than they have, and our workshops move promising people into careers working on them.

  • You’ll build and develop your own programs, lead the teams delivering them, and see the results firsthand.

  • GCP already has a strong brand, an excellent reputation, and a long track record. You’ll build on one of the ecosystem’s most successful workshop programs while joining a team with the ambition to become the leading workshop organizer in the space.

  • You’ll work closely with high-profile guests across AI safety and biorisk, developing a strong professional network.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $140,000–$195,000 (baseline), $175,000–$245,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $195,000–$270,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • Start date: Ideally by October or early November 2026, with flexibility for the right candidate

  • This is a remote role, with travel roughly 8 to 12 times a year (typically 3 to 6 days at a time) for workshops, conferences, and events, predominantly in the UK and US.

  • We’re a remote-first organization, but because of how the GCP team works, we have a preference for candidates within five hours of UK time. Our current team spans GMT-8 to GMT+1, and we’ll gladly consider exceptional candidates elsewhere, including in the US.

  • We may be able to sponsor visas for the UK or US, depending on individual circumstances, including but not limited to O-1A visas. We can’t make guarantees regarding visa approval.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

 

Application Process

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.

  1. Application form (10–20 mins)

  2. Take-home assignment (2–4 hours, paid)

  3. Interview (45 mins)

  4. Reference checks

  5. Work trial (3 days, paid)

  6. Offer

If you’re excited about this role but unsure whether you meet every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. If you’re interested in multiple roles, apply to the one that best fits your skills and interests, and note in your application the other roles that you’d like to be considered for.

This role’s scope, salary, and responsibilities may evolve, and we’ll keep you in the loop about any changes if you apply.

raw.description:
Deliver workshops that help exceptional people pursue high-impact work in AI safety, biosecurity, and policy.

Depending on experience, we consider candidates for the Generalist (Workshops) or Senior Generalist (Workshops) version of this role.

We’re reviewing applications on a rolling basis.


About Kairos

Kairos is a nonprofit accelerating talent into AI safety and policy. In just over two years, we’ve trained 1,200+ people through our flagship programs:

  • SPAR: The largest AI safety research fellowship, with 800+ mentees per round mentored by researchers from Anthropic, Redwood Research, RAND, MIT, the UK AI Security Institute, and others.

  • Generator Residency: In partnership with Constellation, a platform for generalist talent to pitch, build, and ship projects that build capacity and infrastructure across the AI safety ecosystem, with advisors from OpenAI, AI Futures Project, METR, and more.

  • Global Challenges Project: A workshop series introducing promising students to careers in AI safety and biosecurity, run several times a year across Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley.

  • Pathfinder Fellowship: Helping grow the global network of AI safety university groups from a few dozen to nearly 100, with $9.5M in funding over the next two years to support their work.

We see ourselves as a portfolio of highly impactful projects in a fast-evolving field. Over the next six months, we expect to double in size and launch several new initiatives addressing critical gaps in the ecosystem.

 

The Role

The Global Challenges Project (GCP) runs three-day residential workshops that help talented individuals explore careers in AI safety and biosecurity. Over the past few years, GCP has run dozens of workshops for 400+ students, mostly in Oxford, Boston, and Berkeley. GCP has a long and successful track record and became part of Kairos in early 2026.

We’re now expanding GCP into a full portfolio of workshops serving different audiences and career stages, with the ambition of becoming the leading fieldbuilding workshop organizer in AI safety and biosecurity. This means building new programs, new formats, and the systems to deliver reliably at scale.

We’re looking for a generalist to help deliver our workshops. You’ll own the operational backbone of our events, including outreach, venues, travel, admissions logistics, guest coordination, inventory, and the systems that hold it all together. You’ll also attend some of our workshops and help run them in person.

This job requires agency as you’ll own the delivery of many key aspects of our workshops. You’ll need to spot problems before they happen, and improve our strategy and systems after every event. This role offers excellent opportunities for progression, and your scope and responsibility will grow with our portfolio.

 

What You’ll Do

  • Own operational workstreams end to end. For each workshop, you’ll take responsibility for workstreams such as outreach, venue search and contracting, catering and dietary needs, participant and guest travel, inventory and materials, and on-site logistics.

  • Run admissions and participant operations. You’ll build application and RSVP forms, help coordinate selection processes, send decisions, run onboarding communications, and make sure every participant arrives informed and prepared.

  • Coordinate guests. High-quality guests are central to our workshops’ impact. You’ll track invitations, chase confirmations, and act as a point of contact so guests have a smooth experience from first email to follow-up.

  • Deliver workshops in person. You’ll travel to some of our workshops (predominantly in the UK and US) and help run them on the ground.

  • Build systems that scale. We run our events on Notion, Airtable, Linear, and a growing set of automations and custom code. You’ll help design and improve these systems and turn what we learn at each event into better playbooks and templates.

  • Help shape our workshops strategy. You’ll work across GCP, OASIS, and our new workshop programs, and everyone on the team has a say in how Kairos’s events develop.

  • Contribute to Kairos more broadly. As capacity allows, you’ll pitch in on our other programs like SPAR and Pathfinder, build relationships across the AI safety ecosystem, and ship small cross-team projects.

 

Who You Are

  • An operations generalist with events experience. You’ve delivered events such as workshops, conferences, or retreats, or you’ve done demanding operational work and can show you’d thrive doing it for in-person events.

  • Highly organized. You’ll juggle multiple workstreams across several workshops at once, each with its own deadlines. You have strong systems for keeping everything on track, and details don’t slip past you.

  • High agency. You spot problems early and fix them without waiting to be asked, and you adapt when plans change on the day.

  • A high quality bar. You check your own work before handing it over, and you care about getting the small things right because they’re important to the attendees’ experience.

  • Good with people, and energized by workshops. Attending three-day residential events is part of this role. You’ll need the energy to engage warmly with participants and guests while keeping the event running smoothly.

  • Mission-aligned. You care deeply about how the development of advanced AI and biotechnology plays out, and you believe workshops can be a highly effective way to help talented people enter these fields. Familiarity with the AI safety ecosystem is a plus, but not required.

 

Why Work With Us

  • You’ll work toward reducing risks from advanced AI and biotechnology, two of the most important challenges of our time. Both fields need far more talented people than they have, and our workshops move promising people into careers working on them. The quality of our delivery is a big part of that impact.

  • You’ll own your workstreams end to end, and you’ll see the results firsthand at every workshop.

  • You’ll build on GCP’s strong brand, excellent reputation, and long track record, and help us grow into the leading workshop organizer in the space.

  • You’ll work closely with high-profile guests across AI safety and biorisk, and develop a strong professional network.

  • We’re building a world-class team, so you’ll be in good company. Work alongside people who’ve come to Kairos from METR, Coefficient Giving, Rethink Priorities, the UK AI Security Institute, and CEA who share your commitment to impact.

 

What We Offer

  • Salary: $105,000–$145,000 (baseline), $130,000–$180,000 (supported hubs, like London, DC, Boston, and NYC), or $145,000–$200,000 (San Francisco Bay Area), depending on experience, with potential for additional compensation for exceptional candidates

  • Location: This is a remote role. We provide access to office space in San Francisco, Berkeley, London, or Boston, with optional coworking elsewhere. If you work from an AI safety office in one of these cities, we cover food, lunches, and office expenses. If you work from home, we cover home office expenses.

  • Benefits: Flexible working hours, highly competitive health insurance, dental and vision coverage, generous vacation policy, and professional development budget

  • Team retreats: We host all-team retreats three times a year to connect in person, collaborate, and build team culture.

  • Travel: Work-related travel and expenses covered.

 

Logistics

  • This is a remote role, with travel roughly 8 to 12 times a year (typically 3 to 6 days at a time) for workshops, conferences, and events, predominantly in the UK and US.

  • We may be able to sponsor visas for the UK or US, depending on individual circumstances, including but not limited to O-1A visas. We can’t make guarantees regarding visa approval.

 

Our Culture

We’re a small, high-trust team motivated by the urgent challenge of making advanced AI go well. We try hard to figure out where we’re wrong, which means we say uncomfortable things to each other and change our minds fairly often. We value collaborative truth-seeking, a scout mindset, agility, and an alliance mindset with the broader ecosystem.

We also believe meaningful work should be enjoyable. We support each other’s well-being, celebrate wins, and maintain a healthy sense of humor even when the work is hard.

As the Data Scientist in Broker Flow, you'll give the team the evidence behind its product decisions. The core of the work is experiment design and causal inference, with modelling and analysis alongside it.

  • Stochastic methods. You've used stochastic processes for inference or time-series modelling.

  • Broker market insight. You've worked with brokers or other intermediaries in lending or financial services.

description: Managing Director (m/w/d) - Fitness & Lifestyle Brand Location: Köln Start: Ab sofort Setup: Vollzeit (on-site) THE BRAND & THE OPPORTUNITY Du baust gemeinsam mit uns eine neue Fitness-Marke im Segment Mid Cost - High Value auf. Die Vision: „ Der neue Hotspot in der City für Workout, Recovery, Co-Working und Socializing.“ Kraft, Cardio und Functional, Live-Kurse, Sauna und Recovery, Bar und Lounge sowie eine ruhige Co-Working Zone, alles unter einem Dach - zu einem erschwinglichen Preis deutlich unter Premium-Clubs. Unsere Clubs sollen auf ehemaligen Retail-Flächen entstehen, in 1A-Innenstadtlagen mit langfristig gesicherten Mietverträgen. Wir starten in Westdeutschland in der Region Köln, Essen, Frankfurt und expandieren dann. Wir arbeiten mit unternehmerischem Anspruch: kleines Team, kurze Wege, jeder Standort muss sich selbst tragen. Der erste Club ist der Beweis für das Konzept, und jeder weitere wird durch den Erfolg des vorherigen verdient. Für dich heißt das: Du bist ab Sekunde 1 dabei und gestaltest vom Namen über das Konzept bis hin zur Location alles von Grund auf mit. Kein Einstieg in einen bestehenden Betrieb, sondern die Chance, eine Marke von Null an aufzubauen , das Modell in allen Details zu gestalten und volle Verantwortung für das Ergebnis zu übernehmen. THE ROLE & YOUR ROADMAP Als Managing Director verantwortest du den kompletten Aufbau der Marke - von den ersten Entwürfen auf dem Reißbrett bis hin zur Multi-Site-Skalierung. Phase 1 - Konzept schärfen: Du bringst das Angebot, das Flächenprogramm, die Pricing-Strategie und den Brand-Auftritt gemeinsam mit den Gesellschaftern zur Marktreife. Phase 2 - Ersten Club eröffnen: Du steuerst den Ausbau vor Ort, baust dein Kernteam auf, drehst den Pre-Opening-Sales auf Anschlag und bringst den ersten Flagship-Standort ans Netz. Phase 3 - Proof of Concept: Du erreichst mit dem Club die geplanten Mitglieder- und Ergebniszahlen (P&L) und machst aus dem Piloten ein hocheffizientes, wiederholbares Modell. Phase 4 - Skalieren: Du eröffnest weitere Standorte in Deutschland und baust die Organisation auf, die dieses Wachstum trägt. YOUR IMPACT (DIE ERSTEN 12 MONATE) Du bist von Tag 1 an am Start und bringst den ersten Standort ans Netz: Konzept zur Marktreife bringen: Zusammen mit der Projektleitung feilst du an Angebot, Flächenaufteilung, Preisen und Marke. Ausbau steuern: Du betreust den Aus- und Umbau des ersten Standorts und behältst Zeit- und Kostenrahmen fest im Griff. Kernteam aufbauen: Du rekrutierst Club-Leitung, Trainer sowie Servicepersonal und prägst von Anfang an Kultur und Standards. Pre-Sales & Markteintritt verantworten: Du treibst die Mitgliedergewinnung vor der Eröffnung, machst lokales Marketing und schließt Deals mit Firmenkunden sowie Aggregatoren (z. B. Urban Sports Club, EGYM Wellpass). Prozesse & Tech aufsetzen: Du richtest Mitgliederverwaltung, Zugangssysteme, App und Reporting ein. Ersten Club eröffnen: Du begleitest das Grand Opening und führst den Standort erfolgreich in den Live-Betrieb. YOUR PROFILE Du brennst selbst für Fitness und Lifestyle, denkst wie ein Unternehmer und hast den Biss, etwas Eigenes aufzubauen? Dann bist du genau die richtige Person! Track Record: Du hast Führungserfahrung in der Fitnessbranche (z. B. als Area Manager, Cluster Manager oder Regional Director), idealerweise mit P&L Verantwortung. Neueröffnungs-Erfahrung: Du hast schon eine Neueröffnung von A bis Z selbst verantwortet oder mitgestaltet (Ausbau, Teamaufbau, Pre-Sales). Business Mindset: Du hast Kaufmännisches Denken, Data-Drive und souveränes Auftreten gegenüber Gesellschaftern, Vermietern und Partnern. Hands-on & Drive: Du packst überall mit an, bis du zufrieden bist. Danach führst du ein wachsendes Team. Setup: Vollzeit, Wohnsitz oder Relocation in die Startregion Köln, Essen oder Frankfurt. Reisebereitschaft zu den Standorten und Deutsch C2. Das wäre ein Plus: Vorerfahrung aus Hospitality, Wellness oder Gastronomie, Erfahrung im Markenaufbau sowie ein starkes Netzwerk in der Fitnessbranche. WHY US Maximale Gestaltungsfreiheit: Die seltene Chance, eine komplett neue Marke von der ersten Skizze an zu ownen. High-Speed & Support: Kurze Entscheidungswege und direkter Austausch mit den Gesellschaftern. Du entscheidest alles mit! Executive Package: Attraktive Vergütung bestehend aus Fixgehalt, transparentem Bonus und einem Firmenwagen. Contact: Alex Berwanger Find Jobs in Germany on Arbeitnow

title: Embedded Software Entwickler (m/w/d)
description: Du möchtest nicht nur Software entwickeln, sondern direkt erleben, wie dein Code reale Systeme steuert und weiterentwickelt ? Dann könnte diese Position genau das Richtige für dich sein. Unser Kunde entwickelt und fertigt autonome Drohnensysteme, Einsatzsoftware und spezialisierte Lösungen für Industrie, Netzbetreiber, Behörden und maritime Anwendungen. Dabei entstehen hochspezialisierte Systeme, die Hardware, Software und autonome Technologien miteinander verbinden und bereits bei namhaften Kunden zum Einsatz kommen. Für die Weiterentwicklung der Drohnensysteme wird eine erfahrene Persönlichkeit gesucht, die Verantwortung für hardwarenahe Software übernimmt, bestehende Systeme weiterentwickelt und gemeinsam mit einem kleinen technischen Team neue Funktionen bis zum Flugtest bringt. Deine Benefits Attraktive Vergütung: Ein leistungsgerechtes Fixgehalt, das deiner Erfahrung und Qualifikation entspricht. Gestaltungsspielraum: Hohe Eigenverantwortung bei der Weiterentwicklung zentraler Softwarekomponenten und technischen Strukturen. Entwicklungsperspektive: Perspektivisch besteht die Möglichkeit, fachliche Verantwortung für das Softwareteam zu übernehmen. Technologieumfeld: Arbeit an innovativen Drohnensystemen, Embedded Software und autonomen Technologien mit direktem Bezug zur Hardware. Praxisnähe: Kurze Wege von der Entwicklung zum Flugtest und die Möglichkeit, neue Funktionen direkt im realen System zu erproben. Flexibilität: Nach der Einarbeitung ist Homeoffice nach Absprache möglich, wobei die regelmäßige Arbeit an Hardware eine Präsenz vor Ort erforderlich macht. Arbeitsumfeld: Eigene Werkstatt und Testgelände sowie moderne Hard und Software für die Entwicklung und Erprobung. Unternehmenskultur: Kurze Entscheidungswege, direkte Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und eine offene Du Kultur. Teamspirit: Regelmäßige gemeinsame Aktivitäten und Teamevents sorgen für ein persönliches und unkompliziertes Miteinander. Individuelle Benefits: Persönliche Wünsche und Vorschläge sind willkommen. Gemeinsam werden individuelle Benefits erarbeitet. Deine Aufgaben Als Embedded Software Entwickler übernimmst du eine zentrale Rolle bei der Weiterentwicklung der Flugsteuerungs- und Bedienersoftware unserer Drohnensysteme. Flight Control: Technische Verantwortung für die Weiterentwicklung der Flugsteuerungssoftware und deren zuverlässigen Betrieb auf der Zielhardware. Bodenkontrollsoftware: Weiterentwicklung einer modernen Bedienersoftware auf Basis von Qt und QML für Missionsplanung, Drohnenüberwachung und Nutzlaststeuerung. Codebasis: Einarbeitung in bestehende Softwarestrukturen, Dokumentation der Architektur sowie Aufbau sauberer Prozesse für Tests, Releases und Updates. Hardwareintegration: Anbindung und Integration von Sensoren, Funkmodulen, Kameras, Ladesystemen und weiteren Nutzlasten. Debugging: Analyse von Fluglogs, Auswertung technischer Daten und systematische Fehlersuche direkt auf der Zielhardware. Flugerprobung: Begleitung und Durchführung von Flugtests sowie technische Unterstützung bei Erprobungen und gelegentlichen Kundeneinsätzen. Technische Leitung: Fachliche Betreuung eines Auszubildenden und von Werkstudenten, Durchführung von Code Reviews und aktive Weitergabe von Wissen. Architektur: Mitarbeit an technischen Architekturentscheidungen in enger Abstimmung mit der Geschäftsführung. Zusammenarbeit: Enge Abstimmung mit Hardwareentwicklung, Konstruktion und Werkstatt, um Software und Gesamtsystem gemeinsam weiterzuentwickeln. Dein Profil als Embedded Software Entwickler Mindestens fünf Jahre Berufserfahrung in der Softwareentwicklung, davon überwiegend im Embedded Bereich oder in der hardwarenahen C und C++ Entwicklung. Sehr gute praktische Kenntnisse in modernem C++, Qt und QML . Sowie Linux und Git. Erfahrung darin, sich selbstständig in umfangreiche bestehende Codebasen einzuarbeiten und komplexe Softwarestrukturen schnell zu verstehen. Fundierte Erfahrung im hardwarenahen Debugging , insbesondere mit Sensoren, Schnittstellen wie UART, CAN, SPI oder I2C sowie der Analyse von Logs und Fehlerbildern auf Zielhardware. Strukturierte und eigenständige Arbeitsweise sowie die Bereitschaft, technische Lösungen und Wissen nachvollziehbar zu dokumentieren und weiterzugeben. Freude an der Zusammenarbeit mit Hardwareentwicklung und technischen Fachbereichen sowie Interesse daran, Software direkt am realen System zu testen. Bereitschaft zur regelmäßigen Arbeit vor Ort sowie zur Teilnahme an Flugtests und gelegentlichen Kundeneinsätzen. Fließende Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse Nice to have Kenntnisse in ArduPilot oder PX4, MAVLink oder DroneCAN. Wissen in Regelungstechnik, Zustandsschätzung oder Navigation, beispielsweise mit EKF, GNSS oder RTK. Erfahrung mit Open Source Projekten und ein entsprechendes GitHub Profil. Erste Erfahrung als technischer Lead oder im Mentoring jüngerer Entwickler. Erfahrung mit Luftfahrt oder Verteidigungsprojekten sowie Kenntnisse relevanter Safety Standards. Praktische Drohnen Flugerfahrung oder EU Kompetenznachweis A1/A3 beziehungsweise A2. Klingt nach deiner nächsten Herausforderung? Wenn du Embedded Software nicht nur entwickeln, sondern direkt in innovativen Drohnensystemen zum Einsatz bringen möchtest und dabei echte technische Verantwortung übernehmen willst, freuen wir uns auf deinen Lebenslauf. title: Equipment Engineer - Automation
description:
Brief info about Vinted 

Our mission is to make second-hand the first choice, and we're looking for people who want to help us get there. Every day, we work together to help our members buy and sell pre-loved clothing and lifestyle items, giving each piece a second life – or even a third.
The Vinted Group is made up of three business units that support this mission:

Vinted Marketplace is Europe’s leading platform for second-hand fashion and a go-to destination for all kinds of pre-loved items, with a growing range of categories. Our platform connects millions of members across 20+ markets, helping great items find a new life.

Vinted Go enhances the shipping experience with a vast network of over 500,000 pick-up and drop-off points, partnering with more than 60 carriers across Europe, with added services like item verification for peace of mind on high-value pieces.

Vinted Pay is the newest part of the Vinted Group, dedicated to bringing secure, reliable payments to buyers and sellers across Europe. Seamlessly integrated into the Vinted app, it helps keep every transaction safe, efficient, and easy for our members.

Founded in 2008 in Lithuania, Vinted began as a way for friends to find new homes for clothes they no longer needed. In 2019, we became Lithuania's first unicorn! Today, our headquarters remain in Vilnius, and we've grown with offices across Europe, supported by a team of over 2,000 people. 

Missions and activities of the position

1. Project phase – owner's engineer for Maintenance

  • Represent Maintenance in every phase of new equipment projects (starting with the MRS1 cross-belt sorter), from design reviews to FAT, SAT, commissioning and ramp-up. For the sorter, whose design is already set, take over the installed system and optimise it after go-live.
  • Work side by side with the OEM / integrator engineers: collect technical knowledge, challenge design choices, maintainability, access, spare-part strategy and the proposed maintenance plan before they are frozen.
  • Define and verify the Maintenance acceptance criteria (documentation, training, spare parts, safety, availability targets). The Maintenance sign-off is mandatory: no handover to operations without it.
  • Track and drive to closure the technical punch list and warranty issues raised during commissioning and the warranty period.

2. Technical file & spare parts

  • Build and own the equipment technical file: as-built electrical and mechanical drawings, PLC and software versions, parameter backups, network architecture, safety documentation, OEM manuals.
  • Create the asset hierarchy and criticality analysis in the CMMS.
  • Define the critical spare-parts list (references, min/max stock, lead times) and keep it up to date.
  • Reduce dependency on the OEM: identify and qualify second-source suppliers for critical parts, run compatibility tests and document equivalences.
  • Propose spare-parts and supplier decisions to the Maintenance Manager; after an initial period, take these decisions autonomously within agreed limits, with the Maintenance Manager's validation.

3. Maintenance strategy & procedures

  • Write and maintain preventive maintenance plans, corrective procedures and troubleshooting guides for the equipment family, based on OEM data, FMEA and field experience.
  • Monitor equipment performance (availability, MTBF, MTTR, top failure modes), lead root-cause analysis on recurring or major failures and implement permanent corrective actions.
  • Challenge the original design when needed and drive engineering changes: retrofits, drive and firmware updates, software or parameter optimisation, with the OEM and internal stakeholders.

4. Training & technical support

  • Train the operational maintenance team (technicians and operatives) on the equipment, its software/HMI and the troubleshooting procedures; validate their autonomy level.
  • Act as the level-2 / level-3 technical expert for the equipment family on site and remotely, across sites.

5. Escalation, vendor & SLA management

  • Own technical escalations through to resolution: with the Tetris team (Vinted's internal tools and sorting logic) when the issue is on the software or data side, and with OEM / integrator support (SAV) when it is on the equipment side.
  • Lead the diagnosis that tells which side an issue comes from (equipment, controls, Vinted software), with facts and data.
  • Work within the after-sales and maintenance agreements already in place with OEMs: make the most of them day to day, monitor performance against SLAs and warranty terms, feed lessons learned into future renewals, and provide the technical evidence to the program managers, who own the contractual relationship.
  • Prepare and lead technical review meetings with OEMs and integrators.

6. Safety & compliance

  • Ensure the equipment and its maintenance comply with machine safety requirements (CE marking, safety functions, lock-out/tag-out) and site H&S standards.
  • Support safety audits and regulatory inspections, and drive the resulting corrective actions to completion.

Occasional responsibilities

  • Take ownership of additional equipment families (e.g. conveyors, AMR fleets, Monk lines) once the cross-belt is stable.
  • Support pre-project technical due diligence on new equipment (specifications, vendor benchmarks, maintainability review).
  • Participate in the hiring and onboarding of maintenance technicians and future engineers.

Interests, constraints, difficulties of the position

  • High-visibility role on new strategic automation investments.
  • Site-based in an operational warehouse, with regular presence on the shop floor.
  • Regular travel to MRS1, OEM premises (FAT) and other Vinted Go sites, especially during commissioning.
  • Day-based role, no on-call. Flexibility needed during commissioning, ramp-up and major incidents (possible early, late or weekend work).
  • Needs to influence without authority: OEMs, integrators, IT and program management teams.

 

Your profile

Knowledge & experience

  • Engineering degree (Master's / Bac+5) in automation, electrical, mechatronics or industrial engineering, or Bac+2/3 with equivalent proven experience.
  • At least 3 years' experience, ideally 5 or more, as Equipment Engineer, Automation Engineer, Tool Owner or Maintenance/Reliability Engineer in a highly automated environment: parcel sortation and intralogistics, airport baggage handling, logistics or other automated industries.
  • Automation background required.
  • Proven involvement in at least one industrial equipment project from FAT/SAT to ramp-up, working with OEMs or integrators.

Technical skills

  • Able to read and diagnose complete PLC and HMI programs (Siemens TIA Portal and/or Rockwell, Beckhoff) and to make controlled modifications; industrial networks (Profinet, Profibus, EtherCAT, Ethernet/IP).
  • Drives (parameters, firmware), servo motors, sensors, scanners / DWS, pneumatics; reading electrical and mechanical schematics.
  • Retrofit experience and component qualification (equivalence, compatibility testing)
  • Safety PLCs and machine safety functions.
  • Understanding of the interfaces between equipment controls, SCADA/WCS and IT systems.
  • Reliability methods: FMEA, RCA (5 Why, Ishikawa, 8D), criticality analysis; CMMS and PM planning.
  • Sortation equipment experience (cross-belt, tilt-tray, shoe sorters) is a strong plus.
  • French electrical certification (habilitation électrique BR / B2V / BC) or ability to obtain it.
  • Fluent French and professional English (OEMs and the Vinted Go network work in English).

Behavioural skills

  • Strong ownership: treats the equipment as their own, from design to end of life.
  • Able to challenge OEM and integrator engineers constructively, with facts and data.
  • Structured and disciplined in documentation.
  • Good teacher: enjoys transferring knowledge to technicians.
  • Calm and solution-oriented under production pressure; strong safety mindset.


Please note: the main tasks and skills identified and noted in the function described above may need to evolve depending on the constraints and organisation specific to the company and its environment. They are, therefore, indicative and not contractual.


Working at Vinted 

Individual learning budget

Each year, you’ll be given a learning budget (starting at €3,000), and a total of up to 10 working days over a 2-year period to support your personal and professional development.

Equal opportunity

We welcome applications from everybody, regardless of your background, identity, or life experiences. Job openings come with guides, not checklists. If you’re excited about a role, but don’t identify with every point in the ‘About you’ section, apply anyway – you might still be the perfect match!

The annual gross salary range for this position is:
€45.000—€60.000 EUR

title: Solutions Architect - EMEA
description:
About Us

AI coding is the largest use case of enterprise AI adoption today, as is evident from the success of Anthropic on Claude Code, Cursor’s $60B exit to SpaceX, and Cognition’s $48B valuation.

The bottleneck now has moved from code generation to security and safety - AI agents write code faster than any team can review it, and over 65% of the lines of code produced by them are insecure. Vulnerabilities are piling up 16x faster than companies can fix them, and adversaries are able to exploit these new vulnerabilities within hours.

AURI by Endor Labs closes that gap. It runs inside the harness where coding agents work, through hooks, skills and MCP, so the controls sit outside the model and every agent action is visible. Underneath is our patented code context graph, which maps code, open source, containers and infrastructure. It shows which vulnerabilities can actually be reached and exploited, then delivers fixes that won’t break the application. Security teams get evidence instead of noise, and developers get fixes instead of tickets.

The companies building AI trust us to secure it - our customers include OpenAI, SpaceX, DoorDash, Dropbox, Atlassian, MongoDB, Snowflake, Robinhood and Peloton to name a few.

Endor Labs is the third company from Founder & CEO Varun Badhwar, who built Prisma Cloud, the platform that helped define cloud security, from $0 to $300M ARR at Palo Alto Networks. We’ve raised $163M from Lightspeed, Coatue, DFJ Growth, Salesforce Ventures and Dell Technologies Capital.

Software runs everything around our lives today - banking, hospitals, airports and power grids. AI now writes more of it every day, and our mission is to make sure the world can trust that software. Come build that future with us.

How You’ll Make an Impact

As a Solutions Architect at Endor Labs, you're at the heart of connecting our innovative team with our diverse and dynamic customers. Every day presents a new set of exciting challenges and opportunities to make a significant impact:

  • Educate with Enthusiasm: Elevate awareness about Application Security and Software Supply Chain Security. It's about making security engaging and accessible to developers everywhere.
  • Master Our Tech: Deep dive into our supply chain security product suite and emerge as the go-to expert and evangelist.
  • Deliver Tailored Demos: Showcase our solutions in a way that speaks directly to the needs and challenges of our customers. Be the architect of captivating, solution-oriented presentations.
  • Shape Customer Outcomes: Collaborate with our engineering and product teams to design solutions that genuinely address customer challenges. Your insights from the field will directly influence our product development, ensuring we always meet our customers' evolving needs.
  • Facilitate Customer Success: Guide customers through onboarding, ensuring a smooth transition and adoption of the Endor Labs solution. Your goal is to empower customers to leverage our technology fully and ensure they achieve their security and development objectives.

What You Bring to the Table

We're on the hunt for someone who is not just looking for a job but likes a bit of adventure, too! You'll fit right in if you have:

  • Rich Experience: You have experience in pre-sales or a similar customer-facing, technical role. You're no stranger to technical deep dives, product demonstrations, and leading evaluations.
  • Strong Technical Foundation: A solid understanding of modern software development practices, including backend or full-stack development experience, CI/CD pipelines, Git-based development workflows, and DevOps tooling. You’re comfortable engaging deeply with engineering teams and understanding how modern applications are built and deployed.
  • Application Security Awareness: Familiarity with application security concepts, software supply chain security, and/or identity & access management principles. You understand the importance of securing developer workflows and modern cloud-native environments.
  • Tech Savvy: A robust understanding of the Developer, DevOps, Application Security, and open-source ecosystems. Hopefully, you can meet developers where they are and flex some programming skills.
  • Customer & Sales Skills: You've successfully engaged with technical customers at an Enterprise level and know how to articulate complex solutions and operate in a sales cycle.
  • Curious and Eager to Learn: Always on the lookout for new technologies and understanding the intricacies of how things work.
  • Collaborative Spirit: You thrive in a team setting and value diversity and inclusion in every interaction.
  • Action-oriented: You prefer actively solving customer problems and asking for help as needed.

What Makes Us... Us

  • Go to extraordinary lengths to distinguish ourselves through world-class work.
  • Prioritize quality over speed, and speed over scope.
  • Desire to work with deeply kind, mission-driven people.
  • Strive to make the complex simple.
  • Use first principles to debate ideas, test assumptions, and make decisions.
  • Seek the truth by putting data above opinions.
  • Assume good intent and give tactical feedback to help each other get better.
  • Hold no ego—when our customers win, we all win.

What We Offer You

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package including Health, Dental, Vision and Mental Health plans. 
  • 401(k) plan to support your longterm financial goals.
  • Flexible PTO to maintain a healthy work-life balance (we want you here for the long-haul!)
  • Opportunities for co-working and team meetups to foster collaboration.
  • A dog-friendly office environment for those who love to bring their fur babies along.

Endor Labs is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. Even if you don't fit every requirement above, we believe in the power of diverse perspectives and experiences, so we encourage all talented individuals to apply—there's no one-size-fits-all here.

Compensation: For candidates who receive an offer for this position, the compensation range is expected to be between $190,000 - $250,000. This may include additional incentives such as commission targets, restricted stock units, and/or bonuses, depending on the role.

Central Functions is formed of the teams and people that serve the entire business. These people are integral to the smooth running of the business; ensuring everyone is paid on time, that materials are sourced and arrive promptly, that we meet our legal obligations and that our health, safety, and security is safeguarded.

Why be the Data Engineering Lead at THG? 

THG is building the data engineering capability that will underpin everything from daily trading analytics to AI-driven personalisation. As Engineering Lead, you will own the technical vision and delivery for how THG structures, stores and distributes its data across three core domains: Customer, Commercial and Operations.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role. You will be managing and mentoring a team of six engineers (three Senior, three mid-level, each domain-aligned), but you are also expected to be technically deep — setting architecture standards, making key design decisions, and being the person the team turns to when problems are hard.

Your primary mission is to move THG from a fragmented, siloed data landscape towards consistent, joined-up domain datasets that can be trusted and used at scale. We have customer data in multiple places, commercial data that isn't consistently structured, and operational data that isn't easy to consume. You will build the engineering foundation that changes that — working to a shared architecture that ensures Customer, Commercial and Operations datasets have consistent standards, shared attributes where appropriate, and can ultimately be joined into a single, reliable view of the business.

You will work closely with Ingenuity, our technology partner, who manage the foundational platform and first-layer pipelines. Your job is to take what Ingenuity provides and shape it into the structured, high-quality domain datasets that analytics and data science teams can confidently build on. You will also be a key partner to the Data Governance Lead, implementing the standards they define within your engineering practice.

What you'll do:

Technical Leadership & Architecture

  • Own the data engineering architecture for THG — defining how data is ingested, transformed, stored and made available across Customer, Commercial and Operations domains
  • Design consistent standards and patterns across all three domains — ensuring shared attributes are handled uniformly and that data can be reliably joined across domains
  • Lead the evolution of our BigQuery/GCP platform — driving migrations, modernising legacy pipelines, and building for scalability
  • Make key architectural decisions and be accountable for the technical quality of everything the engineering team produces
  • Develop and enforce engineering standards across the team — version control, testing frameworks, error handling, documentation and code review practices

Domain Dataset Development

  • Lead the build-out of structured, reliable domain datasets — moving from disparate, siloed data sources towards consolidated Customer, Commercial and Operations data platforms
  • Work towards the foundations of a single source of truth — defining how data from different source systems is reconciled, deduplicated and mastered within each domain
  • Ensure domain datasets are structured for downstream consumption — analytics teams, data science models, BI tooling and AI/agent use cases should all be able to reliably consume what engineering produces

AI-Enabled Engineering

  • Champion the use of AI in data engineering — this is a small team with a large remit, and we expect AI-assisted development to be embedded in how we work
  • Apply AI tools to accelerate pipeline development, automated testing, anomaly detection and data quality monitoring
  • Stay current with AI developments in the data engineering space and bring new approaches into the team's practice

Ingenuity Relationship

  • Work closely with the Ingenuity engineering team — understanding what they provide at the platform layer and building effectively on top of it
  • Define clear requirements and interface standards for how Ingenuity data feeds into PLC domain datasets
  • Identify and escalate where Ingen platform behaviour affects data quality or availability within PLC domains

People & Team

  • Manage, coach and develop a team of six domain-aligned engineers — three Senior Data Engineers and three Data Engineers
  • Run a structured review and development process for each engineer, building their technical capability and career progression
  • Foster a culture of engineering excellence, collaboration and continuous improvement

What skills and experience do I need for this role?

Essential

  • Hands-on, expert-level experience with BigQuery and GCP — this is non-negotiable; you must have built and operated production data pipelines on this stack
  • Strong Python skills — used daily for pipeline development, data transformation and automation
  • Experience across at least two of the three core data domains: Customer, Commercial and Operations
  • A track record of evolving data architecture — you can demonstrate concrete examples of how you changed the way a business structures, stores or consumes its data
  • Deep understanding of data modelling, pipeline design and distributed data architecture
  • Experience with Dataform or dbt for data transformation
  • Demonstrated use of AI in data engineering — AI-assisted pipeline development, automated quality checks, or similar practical applications
  • Experience mentoring and developing engineers

Desirable

  • Experience building towards a Customer Data Platform (CDP) or equivalent customer data consolidation project
  • Familiarity with data governance principles and working alongside a governance function
  • E-commerce or retail background
  • Experience with streaming or real-time data pipelines

  • Enhanced maternity and paternity pay, depending on length of service.

  • State-of-the-art on-site gym.

Other Perks

The Role: 

We are looking for a Staff QA Engineer to join our team building post-quantum cryptography (PQC) hardware acceleration for HSM and network-appliance products. You will own product-level quality assurance: the system test plans, automation and compliance test execution that stand between an engineering release and a product customers can trust. In a security product, QA is not an afterthought; it is part of the evidence.

Responsibilities:

You will define and execute system-level test plans for FPGA-based cryptographic products: functional, performance, stress, stability and negative testing across the full stack, from hardware through firmware and drivers to cryptographic APIs. You will build and maintain the automated QA infrastructure (regression suites, hardware-in-the-loop test benches, CI integration, results dashboards), execute standards-based compliance test campaigns (NIST ACVP/CAVP test vectors, FIPS 140-3 evidence runs, CNSA 2.0 checklists and standard FPGA compliance tests) together with our verification and security engineers, run interoperability testing against protocol stacks and customer-representative configurations, own defect tracking and triage, and define the release-qualification criteria for every product release.

  • Own system-level QA of cryptographic hardware products: test plans, automation, execution and release qualification
  • Execute standards and compliance test campaigns (ACVP/CAVP vectors, FIPS 140-3 evidence, CNSA 2.0 and FPGA compliance tests) as part of the certification effort

Exposure to security or compliance testing (FIPS, Common Criteria, or telecom/industrial certification regimes) is a strong plus, as is experience testing cryptographic or networking functionality. You are rigorous, methodical and precise in documentation, because in this product your test reports become certification evidence. Fluency in English is required; French or German is an advantage.

  • Experienced system-test/QA engineer for embedded or hardware products with strong automation skills

raw.title: Senior Application Security Engineer
raw.description:
Our mission

We're making Africa the first cashless continent.

In 2017, over half the population in Sub-Saharan Africa had no bank account. That's for good reason—the fees are too high, the closest branch can be miles away, and nobody takes cards. Without access to financial institutions, people are forced to keep their savings under the mattress. Small business owners rely on lenders who charge extortionate rates. Parents spend hours waiting in line to pay school fees in cash.

We're solving this by building financial services that just work: no account fees, instantly available, and accepted everywhere. In places where electricity, water and roads don't always work, you can still send money with Wave. In 2017, we launched a mobile app in Senegal for cash deposit, withdrawal, and peer-to-peer and business payments. Now, we have millions of users across 9 countries and are growing fast.

Our goal is to make Africa the first cashless continent and that's where you come in...

How you'll help us achieve it

We're looking for an experienced security engineer who's independent, excited about getting things done, and ready to hit the ground running. You'll primarily be responsible for our application security, working with our product teams to work on new systems to enhance our security posture. Our customers trust us with their money, and you'll be at the forefront of making sure we retain that trust!

This broadly scoped role will allow you to get your hands on many different types of security projects, from direct application security to helping our infrastructure team think about security for our databases. 

As we integrate AI-powered agents into our engineering and operations workflows, you'll help define and enforce the guardrails around how we use them safely. This includes securing agentic tooling against prompt injection, excessive permissions, and data exfiltration — and building the policies and technical controls to govern AI usage across the company.

Some experience with common industry certifications like ISO-27001 and PCI-DSS would be beneficial, although you won't be expected to run or oversee audits.

Our to-do list changes constantly, but here are some recent projects:

  • Design our agentic SIEM/SecOps pipelines to evaluate and tune AI-driven triage, alerting, and response automation
  • Secure our MCP integrations against prompt injection, tool misuse, and credential exposure
  • Tune and maintain code security review agents tailored to Wave's codebase, threat model, and regulatory environment
  • Develop internal AI governance standards covering acceptable use, data handling, and audit requirements for LLM-powered tools
  • Centralise application-level login and permissions enforcement including privileged access management
  •  Rework our approach to secrets management with ephemeral secrets and tighter access scopes
  • Security review of our public-facing APIs

Key details

  • You can work remotely from anywhere (between UTC -5 and +4) with reliable internet access.
  • Wave covers travel once per year to one of our operating countries in Africa, as well as a yearly stipend of $1200 to meet with coworkers.
  • Our salaries are competitive and are calculated using a transparent formula. For this role, depending on your level of experience, we offer a salary of up to $185,800 USD (or local equivalent), plus a generous equity.
  • We run performance reviews twice a year and award bonuses or promotions to strong performers who have been with the company for more than six months
  • Major benefits:
    • Subsidized health insurance for you and your dependents and retirement contributions (both vary from country-to-country).
    • 6 months fully paid parental leave and subsidized fertility assistance.
    • Flexible vacation, with most folks taking between 30-40 days per year.
    • $10,000 annual charitable donation matching.
    • Yearly travel to one of our African operating countries.

Requirements

  • Minimum of 7-8 years of professional experience with a minimum of 3-5 years of it spent in a security-related role
  • Strong Experience with Python.
  • Fluent English.

You might be a good fit if you

  • Are excited about finding the right balance between security and velocity. 
  • Have opinions on how to secure agentic AI systems and want to put them into practice
  • Enjoy helping other engineers understand and implement secure patterns.
  • Are not afraid to take on complicated systems.
  • Are excited to work on lots of different security-related work, from audits to code refactors. 
  • Work to make things easier for the next engineer who will touch your code.
  • Always try to improve as a programmer and colleague.
  • Are interested in building governance frameworks for AI usage in a regulated financial services environment
  • Have experimented with LLM-based security tooling and understand both the promise and the failure modes
  • Push through hard problems without giving up.
  • Have experience remediating non-conformities.
  • Are interested in security-focused source code review and penetration testing.
  • Have an interest in growing and mentoring a team.

About Engineering at Wave

You'll report to the Security Team Lead and work closely with the CISO, as part of a small 4 person security team, likely rotating with many of our Product and Platform teams, depending on the project you're working on. Each team is led by a product manager and mentored by a technical lead on the team.

You'll be responsible for your own security projects as well as supporting the engineering organisation on security through advice and design review. We organize things to give you as much ownership as possible, so you'll typically be in charge of your projects from planning to delivery.

Our stack (you only need prior experience with python and cloud technologies, if you need to work with anything else, we'll train you):

  • backend: Python 3 (+ mypy)
  • API layer: GraphQL
  • Android frontend: Kotlin/Jetpack
  • iOS frontend: Swift/SwiftUI
  • web frontend: TypeScript/React
  • database: Postgres
  • infrastructure: GCP / Terraform
  • orchestration: Kubernetes

The payoff is big but you have to be willing to put in the work. Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to lead multiple initiatives simultaneously. Grow with us: We're scaling rapidly, which means new challenges, learning opportunities, and career advancement. Total Rewards At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time. Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here. Flexible Working At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
description: RevenueCat gives app businesses the infrastructure and tools to build, run, and improve their monetization. Since graduating from YC's S18 batch, we've grown into the default monetization platform for mobile. We're in 50%+ of newly shipped subscription apps, we process $16B+ in annual purchase volume, and we help everyone from a solo developer to the OpenAI mobile team understand and grow their revenue. We're a remote-first team of 150+ people across 25+ countries, guided by values we actually practice: Customer Obsession, Always Be Shipping, Own It, and Balance. This isn't the right fit for everyone. The systems you’ll build here manage billions of dollars and touch hundreds of millions of end users, and we don’t take that lightly. You'll be expected to work hard and hold a high bar for what you ship, alongside some of the sharpest, most driven people you've worked with. If that sounds energizing rather than exhausting, keep reading. The Role RevenueCat helps apps of all shapes and sizes make more money across mobile, the web, and a growing list of other platforms like Roku, Amazon, and even AR through support for Vision Pro. As a result, many different types of users log in and use RevenueCat on a day-to-day basis. Product managers, support reps, lifecycle marketers, user acquisition specialists, data analysts, executives: the list goes on. Communicating the growing breadth of use cases supported by RevenueCat in a way that makes sense for all those different types of businesses, apps, and users is a challenge. And that’s where product marketing comes in. We’re looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our growing Product Marketing team led by Francie . Each Senior PMM owns a product area end-to-end, partnering with that area's product managers on positioning, messaging, and go-to-market. This is not a segment-specific role: RevenueCat serves everyone from solo indie developers to top-tier enterprise apps, often through the very same product surface, so you'll craft messaging and channels that flex across that full spectrum. This role is perfect for someone who: Knows APIs and SDKs like their ABCs. Code may not be your craft, but you know how to talk the talk. Software developers are one of our core audiences, and they can smell BS a mile away. You can debug marketing messaging so it resonates with technical audiences, and craft narratives around the 1’s and 0’s that still land with business stakeholders. Captains their own ship. You have a strong bias toward action and you’re not afraid to get your hands dirty on execution. Whether it’s juggling strategic and tactical work or navigating shifting priorities, you thrive on autonomy and love making things happen. Distills collaborative chaos. You’re comfortable raising your hand and getting what you need from a dynamic and technical organization. Whether it’s nudging engineers for product updates or rallying Sales for customer stories, you can navigate the chaos and advocate for what the GTM org needs. Gets excited about the unexpected. At RevenueCat we take shipping seriously, and are constantly adapting our product and strategies to meet the needs of developers. You see changes in direction and shifts in strategy as an opportunity to flex your creative muscles and learn on the fly. Is a little quirky. You love a whimsical side quest and you can see the soft side of software. We pride ourselves in keeping our community on their toes with unique swag, challenges and events. You can play as big a role as you’d like in helping to brainstorm and bring these quirky concepts to life. What You’ll Be Responsible For GTM and adoption campaigns: Own key product areas to deeply understand the features we’re launching and the use cases and needs behind them. Craft compelling communication plans both within the organization, and to existing and prospective customers. Lifecycle campaign building: Working with our marketing operations team to execute insight-based lifecycle campaigns to drive adoption, retention and community. Web page design and optimization: Translate product messaging and customer understanding into visually compelling and highly converting web experiences with the help of our external web development agency. You’ll chart the vision for the story our website tells and the illustrations, animations and tools we create to convey it. Case studies and testimonials: Organizing, facilitating, and translating customer interviews into compelling case studies and testimonials that showcase the value of RevenueCat. Internal enablement: As an expert in your areas of product focus, you’ll empower developer-facing teams with the resources and training they need to support developers and ensure their success. Market insights: Keeping your finger on the pulse of the mobile app industry and competitors to inform go-to-market strategies and uncover new opportunities for growth. Whimsical side quests: Taking on unique projects with minimal instruction, coordinating the collection of 1000 screenshots to launch Paywalls.com , designing, printing and shipping a calendar of cat photos, hosting the World Paywall Speed Building Championships , or crafting a keynote speech for leadership. You’ll get to work on projects that stretch your creative muscles. What You’ll Need to Be Successful 5+ years of experience in Product Marketing within a B2B or B2D SaaS environment, preferably targeting developers or software companies. RevenueCat runs a hybrid motion - self-serve/PLG for indie developers alongside a sales-assisted motion for larger accounts - so experience with either end of that spectrum is valuable; you won't need to have done both to succeed here. Previous experience as a solo-marketer is preferred. While you’ll have the broader marketing and product marketing teams to lean on, our async, entrepreneurial culture is best suited to someone who is comfortable independently driving projects forward, making progress amid changing processes, and actively enlisting cross-functional support when needed. Experience owning end-to-end go-to-market efforts, including tier 1 product launches. Strong project management skills to prioritize multiple initiatives and execute effectively across teams. Strong creative instincts and direction. You’ve led the charge on web design work and aren’t afraid to sketch, prototype in Figma, or use AI tools to get to an ugly starting point. Comfortable collaborating with external creative agencies and freelancers to deliver high-quality assets. Excellent editorial judgment: you understand audience, tone, and communication objectives, and you can elevate copy through clear direction and feedback. You will not need to write everything yourself, but you’re comfortable jumping in to draft a narrative outline or even a blog post when necessary, and you know when to pass work forward to the content team or a technical writer Exceptional communication skills to collaborate across technical and non-technical teams, ensuring alignment and buy-in from key stakeholders.
